(a) the analog-spectrum approach is more realistic than the standard one; (b) semidegenerate bases are the most suitable emulators for universal bases; and (c) probe length remains the performance-govering factor.

a novel SBH approach based on the analog-spectrum, which, in contrast to the standard approach, allows the reliable sequencing of longer DNA fragments.
the development of a novel approach to DNA sequencing by the use of microarrays.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by the introduction of semidegenerate bases and the use of the analog-spectrum acquisition model, the length of reliably reconstructed sequences can be increased by a factor of 4.
, for a fixed microarray, the analog-spectrum approach is more robust, more reliable, and more accurate than the standard digital-spectrum one.

, in the analog-spectrum, the sequence-length performance is governed by the probe length, and the sequence-complexity performance is governed by both probe length and the degree of degeneracy of the bases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in SBH, the sequence reconstruction is not the main bottleneck, but the spectrum acquisition.
the analog-spectrum approach can be used for a wide range of probing patterns.

the analog-spectrum approach is capable of delivering m/sub len/ and m/sub comp/ of O(2/super L/) and O(4/super L/), respectively, with a reasonable probe length L, and that the performance is not affected by the presence of gaps in the probing pattern, as long as the gaps are not too large.
